## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(Seurat)
library(Matrix)
library(data.table)

geo_dir  <- "data/raw/geo"
proc_dir <- "data/processed"
dir.create(proc_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

geo_file <- function(...) file.path(geo_dir, paste0("GSE207192_", ...))

# formatting helpers for numbers quoted inline in the prose
fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
fmt_e <- function(x) sprintf("%.1e", x)
```

## Load the processed GEO matrices

GEO provides one RNA matrix and one ADT matrix per stage (pre- and post-infusion), stored as
genes × cells in Matrix Market format. Gene names, protein names and cell barcodes are in separate
one-column CSVs. Both modalities share a single cell barcode file per stage.

```{r}
#| label: load-fn
read_names <- function(path) fread(path, header = TRUE)[[1]]

load_stage <- function(stage) {
  rna <- as(readMM(geo_file(stage, "_Infusion_scRNA_Raw_Counts.mtx.gz")), "CsparseMatrix")
  adt <- as(readMM(geo_file(stage, "_Infusion_ADT_Raw_Counts.mtx.gz")), "CsparseMatrix")

  rna_features <- read_names(geo_file(stage, "_Infusion_scRNA_Raw_Counts_features_rownames.csv.gz"))
  adt_features <- read_names(geo_file(stage, "_Infusion_scADT_Raw_Counts_features_rownames.csv.gz"))
  cells        <- read_names(geo_file(stage, "_Infusion_scADT_and_scRNA_Raw_Counts_cells_colnames.csv.gz"))
  meta         <- fread(geo_file(stage, "_Infusion_scADT_and_scRNA_Raw_Counts_metaData.csv.gz"),
                        colClasses = "character")

  # Dimensions must line up with the name files before we attach names
  stopifnot(
    nrow(rna) == length(rna_features), ncol(rna) == length(cells),
    nrow(adt) == length(adt_features), ncol(adt) == length(cells),
    !anyDuplicated(cells)
  )

  dimnames(rna) <- list(make.unique(rna_features), cells)
  dimnames(adt) <- list(adt_features, cells)

  # Metadata must cover exactly the same cells, in the same order
  stopifnot(identical(meta$cells, cells))
  meta <- as.data.frame(meta)
  rownames(meta) <- meta$cells
  meta$cells <- NULL

  obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = rna, assay = "RNA", project = paste0(stage, "_Infusion"),
                            meta.data = meta)
  obj[["ADT"]] <- CreateAssay5Object(counts = adt)
  obj$stage <- stage
  obj
}
```

```{r}
#| label: load
pre  <- load_stage("Pre")
post <- load_stage("Post")
pre
post
```

```{r}
#| label: feature-checks
# Duplicated gene symbols in the GEO file (made unique with a .1 suffix on load)
raw_genes <- read_names(geo_file("Pre", "_Infusion_scRNA_Raw_Counts_features_rownames.csv.gz"))
raw_genes[duplicated(raw_genes)]

# ADT panel (Seurat swaps any "_" for "-")
rownames(pre[["ADT"]])
# Same 32 proteins in both stages, but in a different order (CD45RA is last in pre, first in post)
setequal(rownames(pre[["ADT"]]), rownames(post[["ADT"]]))
identical(rownames(pre[["ADT"]]), rownames(post[["ADT"]]))
identical(rownames(pre[["RNA"]]), rownames(post[["RNA"]]))

# Cells with no ADT counts at all
sapply(list(pre = pre, post = post), function(o) sum(o$nCount_ADT == 0))
table(post$orig.ident[post$nCount_ADT == 0])
```

## Metadata

```{r}
#| label: metadata
head(pre[[]])
head(post[[]])

table(pre$patientShort, pre$patient)
table(post$patientShort, post$time)
table(pre$Final_celltype)
table(post$Final_celltype)
```

## Cell barcode format

Every barcode should look like `<sample prefix>_<16-nt 10x barcode>-1`.

```{r}
#| label: barcode-format
barcode_re <- "^([^_]+)_([ACGT]{16})-([0-9]+)$"

check_barcodes <- function(obj) {
  bc <- colnames(obj)
  ok <- grepl(barcode_re, bc)
  list(
    n_cells        = length(bc),
    n_bad_format   = sum(!ok),
    gem_suffixes   = table(sub(barcode_re, "\\3", bc[ok])),
    n_dup_core_bc  = sum(duplicated(sub(barcode_re, "\\1_\\2", bc[ok]))),
    prefixes       = table(prefix = sub(barcode_re, "\\1", bc[ok]))
  )
}

check_barcodes(pre)
check_barcodes(post)
```

### Does the barcode prefix agree with the metadata?

Pre-infusion prefixes are the patient ID, but the style varies: `P033`, `P034` and `P049` keep the
"P", while `031`, `039`, `048` and `116` drop it. Post-infusion prefixes follow
`<patient>-<day>-<sort label>` (e.g. `031-d10-CART`).

```{r}
#| label: prefix-vs-meta
pre_prefix <- sub(barcode_re, "\\1", colnames(pre))
table(prefix = pre_prefix, patient = pre$patient)

post_prefix <- sub(barcode_re, "\\1", colnames(post))
post_parts  <- tstrsplit(post_prefix, "-")
post_check  <- data.frame(
  prefix        = post_prefix,
  prefix_pt     = paste0("P", post_parts[[1]]),
  prefix_day    = post_parts[[2]],
  meta_patient  = post$patient,
  meta_time     = post$time
)
post_check$patient_match <- post_check$prefix_pt  == post_check$meta_patient
post_check$day_match     <- post_check$prefix_day == post_check$meta_time

unique(post_check[!(post_check$patient_match & post_check$day_match),
                  c("prefix", "meta_patient", "meta_time")])
table(mismatch = !(post_check$patient_match & post_check$day_match))
```

### Summary of checks

- **Format:** all 23,663 pre-infusion and 55,185 post-infusion barcodes match
  `<prefix>_<16-nt barcode>-1`. Every cell has GEM suffix `-1`, and no barcode is duplicated.
- **Metadata:** cell order in the metadata files matches the matrix columns exactly in both stages.
- **Pre-infusion prefixes:** inconsistent style (`P033` vs `031`), but every prefix maps to one
  patient. The `patient` column has no "P" here (`033`), whereas post-infusion uses `P034`.
- **Pre-infusion P06 (patient 048):** only 4 cells.
- **Post-infusion `028-d04-nonT` (25 cells):** the barcode prefix says patient 028, day 4, but the
  metadata says P034 at d05. These cells also have zero ADT counts. They are the only mismatch
  and are probably a small non-T control sample. Flag them before any per-patient analysis.
- **ADT panel:** the same 32 proteins in both stages, in a different order.

## Match TCR data to the count matrices

The TCR tables come from `cellranger vdj aggr` across all 30 libraries (7 pre-infusion and 23
post-infusion). Aggregation drops the sample prefix and appends a library number instead
(`AAACCTGAGAAGGTGA-1`, `...-2`, …). 10x reuses the same barcode list in every library, so the
16-nt barcode alone does not identify a cell. We have to work out which suffix belongs to which
sample, then join on barcode **plus** suffix.

### Suffix → library map

The contig table records `donor`, `origin` and `Meta:time` for each cell, so the map comes from
the data itself.

```{r}
#| label: tcr-load
contigs <- fread(geo_file("All_TCR_Aggregated_filtered_contig_annotations.csv.gz"))
stopifnot(all(grepl("^[ACGT]{16}-[0-9]+$", contigs$barcode)))
contigs[, `:=`(core = sub("-[0-9]+$", "", barcode),
               sfx  = as.integer(sub("^.*-", "", barcode)))]

# All contigs are already filtered: cells, productive, high-confidence
contigs[, .N, by = .(is_cell, productive, high_confidence, `Meta:celltype`)]

lib_map <- unique(contigs[, .(sfx, donor, time = `Meta:time`, origin)])[order(sfx)]
# Each suffix is one library, and each donor + day is one suffix
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(lib_map$sfx), !anyDuplicated(lib_map[, .(donor, time)]))
lib_map[, n_tcr_cells := contigs[, uniqueN(barcode), by = sfx][lib_map, on = "sfx", V1]]
lib_map
```

Suffixes 1–23 are the post-infusion timepoints and 24–30 are pre-infusion (`d00`), one per
patient.

### Assign each GEX cell its expected suffix

We assign suffixes from the cell metadata (`patient` + `time`, with pre-infusion set to `d00`), not
from the barcode prefix. That matters for the 25 `028-d04-nonT` cells, whose prefix disagrees
with their metadata (see above).

```{r}
#| label: gex-suffix
gex_cells <- function(obj, stage) {
  data.table(
    cell   = colnames(obj),
    stage  = stage,
    prefix = sub(barcode_re, "\\1", colnames(obj)),
    core   = sub(barcode_re, "\\2", colnames(obj)),
    donor  = as.integer(sub("^P", "", obj$patient)),
    time   = if (stage == "Pre") "d00" else obj$time
  )
}
gex <- rbind(gex_cells(pre, "Pre"), gex_cells(post, "Post"))
gex <- lib_map[, .(donor, time, sfx, origin)][gex, on = .(donor, time)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(gex$sfx))

unique(gex[, .(stage, prefix, donor, time, sfx, origin)])[order(sfx)]
```

### Check the map against the barcodes themselves

This check doesn't use the metadata. For each GEX sample, we find the TCR suffix where its
16-nt barcodes most often appear. If the map is right, that suffix should be the one assigned
above.

```{r}
#| label: suffix-crosscheck
tcr_core <- unique(contigs[, .(core, sfx)])
hits <- merge(gex[, .(prefix, core)], tcr_core, by = "core", allow.cartesian = TRUE)

top_hit <- hits[, .N, by = .(prefix, hit_sfx = sfx)
              ][, share := N / sum(N), by = prefix
              ][order(-N)][, .SD[1], by = prefix]

crosscheck <- unique(gex[, .(prefix, sfx, origin)])[top_hit, on = "prefix"]
crosscheck[, agrees := sfx == hit_sfx]
crosscheck[order(sfx), .(prefix, origin, expected_sfx = sfx, top_hit_sfx = hit_sfx,
                         share_on_top = round(share, 3), agrees)]
stopifnot(all(crosscheck$agrees))
```

Every sample's top hit is its expected suffix, typically with ~90% of hits. The rest are chance
barcode collisions with other libraries. This is why a join on the 16-nt barcode alone would be
wrong:

```{r}
#| label: naive-join
cores_per_lib <- tcr_core[, .(n_libs = .N), by = core]
gex[cores_per_lib, n_libs_with_core := i.n_libs, on = "core"]
gex[is.na(n_libs_with_core), n_libs_with_core := 0L]
gex[, tcr_barcode := paste0(core, "-", sfx)]
gex[, has_tcr := tcr_barcode %in% contigs$barcode]

gex[, .(
  gex_cells               = .N,
  naive_match_core_only   = sum(n_libs_with_core > 0),
  core_in_multiple_libs   = sum(n_libs_with_core > 1),
  naive_false_matches     = sum(n_libs_with_core > 0 & !has_tcr),
  correct_match           = sum(has_tcr)
), by = stage]
```

### Join and report match rates

Collapse contigs to one row per cell before joining.

```{r}
#| label: tcr-per-cell
stopifnot(contigs[, uniqueN(raw_clonotype_id), by = barcode][, all(V1 == 1)])
tcr_cells <- contigs[, .(
  tcr_clonotype = raw_clonotype_id[1],
  tcr_n_TRA     = sum(chain == "TRA"),
  tcr_n_TRB     = sum(chain == "TRB"),
  tcr_TRA_cdr3  = paste(cdr3[chain == "TRA"], collapse = ";"),
  tcr_TRB_cdr3  = paste(cdr3[chain == "TRB"], collapse = ";")
), by = .(tcr_barcode = barcode)]
```

**Share of GEX cells with a TCR**, by sample:

```{r}
#| label: match-gex
by_sample <- gex[, .(gex_cells = .N, with_tcr = sum(has_tcr),
                     pct = round(100 * mean(has_tcr), 1)), by = .(stage, origin, sfx)][order(sfx)]
by_sample
gex[, .(gex_cells = .N, with_tcr = sum(has_tcr), pct = round(100 * mean(has_tcr), 1)), by = stage]
gex[, .(gex_cells = .N, with_tcr = sum(has_tcr), pct = round(100 * mean(has_tcr), 1))]
```

**Share of TCR cells found in the count matrices**, by library. TCR cells without a GEX match
were probably removed by the authors' GEX quality filtering.

```{r}
#| label: match-tcr
tcr_cells[, in_gex := tcr_barcode %in% gex$tcr_barcode]
tcr_cells[, sfx := as.integer(sub("^.*-", "", tcr_barcode))]
tcr_side <- tcr_cells[, .(tcr_cells = .N, in_gex = sum(in_gex),
                          pct = round(100 * mean(in_gex), 1)), by = sfx
                    ][lib_map[, .(sfx, origin)], on = "sfx"][order(sfx)]
tcr_side
tcr_cells[, .(tcr_cells = .N, in_gex = sum(in_gex), pct = round(100 * mean(in_gex), 1))]
```

### Attach TCR data to the Seurat objects

```{r}
#| label: tcr-attach
add_tcr <- function(obj) {
  m <- tcr_cells[gex[match(colnames(obj), cell), .(cell, tcr_barcode, tcr_library = origin)],
                 on = "tcr_barcode"]
  stopifnot(identical(m$cell, colnames(obj)))
  m <- as.data.frame(m[, .(tcr_barcode, tcr_library, has_tcr = !is.na(tcr_clonotype),
                           tcr_clonotype, tcr_n_TRA, tcr_n_TRB, tcr_TRA_cdr3, tcr_TRB_cdr3)])
  rownames(m) <- colnames(obj)
  AddMetaData(obj, m)
}
pre  <- add_tcr(pre)
post <- add_tcr(post)

table(pre$has_tcr)
table(post$has_tcr)
```

```{r}
#| label: tcr-cleanup
rm(contigs, tcr_core, hits, top_hit, crosscheck, cores_per_lib, tcr_cells, gex, gex_cells,
   lib_map, by_sample, tcr_side, add_tcr, post_check, post_parts, post_prefix, pre_prefix,
   raw_genes, check_barcodes)
invisible(gc())
```

### TCR matching summary

- **Mapping:** the 30 aggregation suffixes map one-to-one to libraries (1–23 post-infusion, 24–30
  pre-infusion). The barcode-overlap check agrees with the metadata for every GEX sample.
- **`028-d04-nonT`:** its barcodes land on suffix 7 (`034-d05-CART`). That confirms the metadata
  (P034, d05) is right and the barcode prefix is wrong.
- **Match rate:** 68,728 of 78,848 GEX cells (87.2%) have a TCR: pre-infusion 90.4%
  (21,392 / 23,663) and post-infusion 85.8% (47,336 / 55,185). In the other direction, 93.8% of
  TCR cells (68,728 / 73,250) are found in the count matrices.
- **Joining on barcode alone would be wrong:** it would add 926 false matches (203 pre, 723 post),
  where a cell's barcode exists only in another sample's TCR library.
- **Low-match libraries:** `116-d21` (14.3%; only 147 TCR cells for 920 GEX cells), `039-d10`
  (55.7%) and `116-d28` (58.8%). In the first two, almost all TCR cells are in the GEX data,
  so the TCR library itself captured fewer cells. This isn't a joining problem.
  `049-d05-CART` (suffix 16, 2 cells) has no GEX counterpart.

#| cache: false
saveRDS(pre,  file.path(proc_dir, "seurat_pre_infusion.rds"))
saveRDS(post, file.path(proc_dir, "seurat_post_infusion.rds"))

## Quality control

The GEO matrices are already filtered by the authors. Post-infusion cells all have >500 UMIs and
<10% mitochondrial reads. Pre-infusion has no cell below 683 UMIs but allows up to 25% mito.
The two stages also differ a lot in depth: the median is ~13k UMIs per cell pre-infusion vs
~4k post-infusion. So QC here is a light second pass:

- **Low UMIs / low genes:** more than 3 MADs below the sample's median, on a log scale. The cutoff
  is computed per sample because depth varies so much between samples. Samples with <100 cells
  are pooled within their stage.
- **High mito:** a fixed 10% cap in both stages, matching the authors' post-infusion filter.
  Per-sample 3-MAD mito cutoffs land at ~4.5–9.7% and would remove ~3,300 cells. That is
  stricter than the authors and penalises activated T cells, which naturally carry more
  mitochondrial RNA.
- **No ADT counts:** cells with no surface-protein data at all. These are the 25 `028-d04-nonT`
  cells.
- **Doublets:** scDblFinder, run per sample (samples with ≥100 cells only).

### QC metrics

```{r}
#| label: qc-metrics
library(scater)
library(patchwork)
library(scDblFinder)

add_qc <- function(obj) {
  obj[["percent.mt"]]   <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, pattern = "^MT-",       assay = "RNA")
  obj[["percent.ribo"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, pattern = "^RP[SL][0-9]", assay = "RNA")
  iso <- c("IgG1", "IgG2a", "IgG2b")
  adt <- LayerData(obj, assay = "ADT", layer = "counts")
  obj$adt_isotype_counts <- colSums(adt[iso, , drop = FALSE])
  obj$adt_isotype_frac   <- obj$adt_isotype_counts / pmax(obj$nCount_ADT, 1)
  obj
}
pre  <- add_qc(pre)
post <- add_qc(post)

qc_cols <- c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt", "percent.ribo",
             "nCount_ADT", "nFeature_ADT", "adt_isotype_frac")
qc_summary <- function(obj) t(sapply(obj[[]][, qc_cols], function(x)
  round(quantile(x, c(0, 0.01, 0.05, 0.5, 0.95, 0.99, 1)), 2)))
cat("== PRE\n");  print(qc_summary(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(qc_summary(post))
```

```{r}
#| label: qc-per-sample
per_sample <- function(o) {
  d <- data.table(sample = o$orig.ident, n_umi = as.numeric(o$nCount_RNA),
                  n_gene = as.numeric(o$nFeature_RNA), mt = o$percent.mt,
                  adt = as.numeric(o$nCount_ADT), celltype = o$Final_celltype)
  d[, .(cells = .N, med_umi = median(n_umi), med_gene = median(n_gene),
        med_mt = round(median(mt), 2), p99_mt = round(quantile(mt, .99), 1),
        med_adt = median(adt), pct_undet = round(100 * mean(celltype == "undetermined"), 1)),
    by = sample][order(sample)]
}
cat("== PRE\n");  print(per_sample(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(per_sample(post))
```

In pre-infusion, the "P"-prefixed samples (P033, P034, P049) have about twice the median mito % of
the others (~4.4–5.4% vs ~2.2%). Together with the different naming, this suggests two
processing batches. Pre-infusion patient 116 has 25.5% "undetermined" cells, vs ≤1.2% in the other
pre-infusion samples (excluding the 4-cell 048 sample).

### QC flags

```{r}
#| label: qc-flags
max_mt <- 10

qc_flag <- function(obj, min_cells = 100) {
  md  <- obj[[]]
  n   <- table(md$orig.ident)
  # Tiny samples borrow thresholds from the pooled small samples of the stage
  grp <- ifelse(n[as.character(md$orig.ident)] < min_cells, "small_pooled",
                as.character(md$orig.ident))
  low_umi  <- isOutlier(md$nCount_RNA,   nmads = 3, log = TRUE, type = "lower", batch = grp)
  low_gene <- isOutlier(md$nFeature_RNA, nmads = 3, log = TRUE, type = "lower", batch = grp)
  obj$qc_group    <- grp
  obj$qc_low_umi  <- as.logical(low_umi)
  obj$qc_low_gene <- as.logical(low_gene)
  obj$qc_high_mt  <- obj$percent.mt > max_mt
  obj$qc_no_adt   <- obj$nCount_ADT == 0
  thr <- data.table(group    = names(attr(low_umi, "thresholds")["lower", ]),
                    min_umi  = round(attr(low_umi,  "thresholds")["lower", ]),
                    min_gene = round(attr(low_gene, "thresholds")["lower", ]),
                    max_mt   = max_mt)
  list(obj = obj, thresholds = thr)
}

res <- qc_flag(pre);  pre  <- res$obj; thr_pre  <- res$thresholds
res <- qc_flag(post); post <- res$obj; thr_post <- res$thresholds
rm(res); invisible(gc())

flag_cols <- c("qc_low_umi", "qc_low_gene", "qc_high_mt", "qc_no_adt")
flag_summary <- function(o) {
  d <- as.data.table(o[[]][, c("orig.ident", flag_cols)])
  d[, any_flag := qc_low_umi | qc_low_gene | qc_high_mt | qc_no_adt]
  d[, c(.(cells = .N), lapply(.SD, sum), .(pct_flagged = round(100 * mean(any_flag), 1))),
    by = orig.ident, .SDcols = c(flag_cols, "any_flag")][order(orig.ident)]
}
cat("== PRE thresholds\n");  print(thr_pre)
cat("== PRE flags\n");       print(flag_summary(pre))
cat("== POST thresholds\n"); print(thr_post)
cat("== POST flags\n");      print(flag_summary(post))
```

```{r}
#| label: qc-plots
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
qc_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#ebeae6", linewidth = 0.3),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#0b0b0b"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = "#52514e"))

qc_panel <- function(md, cut, col, cut_col, label, log = TRUE) {
  p <- ggplot(md, aes(x = .data[[col]], y = sample)) +
    geom_violin(fill = "#d6d5d0", colour = NA, scale = "width", width = 0.85) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.18, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "#fcfcfb",
                 colour = "#52514e", linewidth = 0.35) +
    geom_point(data = cut, aes(x = .data[[cut_col]]), shape = "|", size = 5, colour = "#eb6834") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) + labs(title = label, x = NULL, y = NULL) + qc_theme
  if (log) p + scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()))
  else p
}

qc_plot <- function(obj, thr, title) {
  md  <- as.data.table(obj[[]])[, .(sample = orig.ident, qc_group,
                                    umi = as.numeric(nCount_RNA), gene = as.numeric(nFeature_RNA),
                                    mt = percent.mt)]
  cut <- unique(md[, .(sample, qc_group)])[thr, on = c(qc_group = "group"), nomatch = 0]
  (qc_panel(md, cut, "umi", "min_umi", "UMIs per cell (log)") |
   qc_panel(md, cut, "gene", "min_gene", "Genes per cell (log)") + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank()) |
   qc_panel(md, cut, "mt", "max_mt", "Mito %", log = FALSE) + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())) +
    plot_annotation(title = title, subtitle = "Orange tick = QC cutoff for that sample",
                    theme = qc_theme)
}

qc_plot(pre,  thr_pre,  "Pre-infusion QC")
qc_plot(post, thr_post, "Post-infusion QC")
```

### Doublets

```{r}
#| label: doublets
run_dbl <- function(obj, min_cells = 100) {
  n    <- table(obj$orig.ident)
  keep <- as.character(obj$orig.ident) %in% names(n)[n >= min_cells]
  sce  <- SingleCellExperiment(list(counts = LayerData(obj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")[, keep]))
  set.seed(1)
  sce  <- scDblFinder(sce, samples = as.character(obj$orig.ident[keep]),
                      BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam())
  obj$dbl_class <- "not_run"
  obj$dbl_score <- NA_real_
  obj$dbl_class[keep] <- as.character(sce$scDblFinder.class)
  obj$dbl_score[keep] <- sce$scDblFinder.score
  rm(sce); invisible(gc())
  obj
}
pre  <- run_dbl(pre)
post <- run_dbl(post)

dbl_summary <- function(o) {
  d <- as.data.table(o[[]])[, .(sample = orig.ident, dbl_class, multi_TRB = tcr_n_TRB >= 2)]
  d[, .(cells = .N, doublets = sum(dbl_class == "doublet"),
        pct_dbl = round(100 * mean(dbl_class == "doublet"), 1),
        not_run = sum(dbl_class == "not_run")), by = sample][order(sample)]
}
cat("== PRE\n");  print(dbl_summary(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(dbl_summary(post))
```

scDblFinder calls 2–9% of cells doublets per sample. As a check that doesn't depend on the
expression data, cells with two or more TCR beta chains, a common sign of a doublet, should be
called doublets much more often:

```{r}
#| label: doublet-tcr-check
dbl_vs_trb <- function(o) {
  d <- as.data.table(o[[]])[has_tcr == TRUE & dbl_class != "not_run",
                            .(multi_TRB = tcr_n_TRB >= 2, doublet = dbl_class == "doublet")]
  d[, .(cells = .N, pct_doublet = round(100 * mean(doublet), 1)), by = multi_TRB][order(multi_TRB)]
}
cat("== PRE\n");  print(dbl_vs_trb(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(dbl_vs_trb(post))
```

They are: about 47–49% of multi-TRB cells are called doublets, vs 2–4% of other cells. Multi-TRB
cells that scDblFinder did not call doublets are kept, since a small share of T cells carry
two beta chains.

### Filter

```{r}
#| label: qc-pass
set_qc_pass <- function(o) {
  o$qc_pass <- !(o$qc_low_umi | o$qc_low_gene | o$qc_high_mt | o$qc_no_adt) &
    o$dbl_class != "doublet"
  o
}
pre  <- set_qc_pass(pre)
post <- set_qc_pass(post)

pass_summary <- function(o) {
  d <- as.data.table(o[[]])
  out <- d[, .(cells = .N, kept = sum(qc_pass), removed = sum(!qc_pass),
               pct_kept = round(100 * mean(qc_pass), 1)), by = orig.ident][order(orig.ident)]
  rbind(out, d[, .(orig.ident = "TOTAL", cells = .N, kept = sum(qc_pass), removed = sum(!qc_pass),
                   pct_kept = round(100 * mean(qc_pass), 1))])
}
cat("== PRE\n");  print(pass_summary(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(pass_summary(post))
```

Save every cell's QC flags before dropping any, so the filtering decisions stay on record:

```{r}
#| label: qc-save-flags
#| cache: false
flag_export <- c("orig.ident", "stage", "nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt", "percent.ribo",
                 "nCount_ADT", "qc_group", "qc_low_umi", "qc_low_gene", "qc_high_mt", "qc_no_adt",
                 "dbl_class", "dbl_score", "qc_pass")
qc_flags <- rbind(data.table(cell = colnames(pre),  pre[[]][, flag_export]),
                  data.table(cell = colnames(post), post[[]][, flag_export]))
fwrite(qc_flags, file.path(proc_dir, "qc_flags.csv.gz"))
rm(qc_flags, flag_export); invisible(gc())
```

```{r}
#| label: qc-filter
pre  <- subset(pre,  cells = colnames(pre)[pre$qc_pass])
post <- subset(post, cells = colnames(post)[post$qc_pass])
invisible(gc())
c(pre = ncol(pre), post = ncol(post))
```

### QC summary

- **Kept:** pre-infusion `r fmt_n(ncol(pre))` of 23,663 cells (`r round(100*ncol(pre)/23663,1)`%), post-infusion `r fmt_n(ncol(post))` of 55,185 (`r round(100*ncol(post)/55185,1)`%).
  Per sample, 84.7–96.1% is kept, ignoring the 4- and 20-cell samples.
- **Removed:** all 25 `028-d04-nonT` cells (no ADT data).
- **Doublet check:** the doublet calls agree with the TCR data (see above).
- **For later steps:** depth differs ~3× between stages, and pre-infusion looks like it was
  processed in two batches (P-prefixed samples have higher mito). Both matter for integration.

## Normalize

RNA uses LogNormalize (scale factor 10,000). SCTransform was ruled out to keep memory use
manageable on a 16 GB machine. ADT uses CLR across each cell's proteins (`margin = 2`), the
standard Seurat method for antibody counts.

```{r}
#| label: normalize
normalize <- function(o) {
  o <- NormalizeData(o, assay = "RNA", normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
                     scale.factor = 1e4, verbose = FALSE)
  o <- NormalizeData(o, assay = "ADT", normalization.method = "CLR", margin = 2, verbose = FALSE)
  o
}
pre  <- normalize(pre)
post <- normalize(post)
invisible(gc())
```

```{r}
#| label: qc-cleanup
rm(add_qc, qc_cols, qc_summary, per_sample, qc_flag, flag_cols, flag_summary, thr_pre, thr_post,
   max_mt, qc_theme, qc_panel, qc_plot, run_dbl, dbl_summary, dbl_vs_trb, set_qc_pass,
   pass_summary, normalize)
invisible(gc())
```

## VDJ QC

The TCR columns attached earlier used every contig. Here they're rebuilt from contigs that pass
contig-level QC:

- **Contig flags:** `productive`, `full_length`, `high_confidence` and `is_cell` all TRUE.
- **UMI support:** at least 2 UMIs per contig (3 for a noisy run; see the check below).
- **Chain counts:** up to 2 TRA is normal (weak allelic exclusion). A cell with more than 1 TRB,
  or more than 2 TRA, is flagged as a likely doublet (`tcr_multichain`). Its chains are kept, and
  each cell's top-UMI TRA and TRB are stored separately (`tcr_TRA1_*`, `tcr_TRB1_*`).
- **Barcode matching:** only cells that passed GEX QC are kept (`pre` and `post` are already
  filtered).

```{r}
#| label: vdj-load
contigs <- fread(geo_file("All_TCR_Aggregated_filtered_contig_annotations.csv.gz"),
                 select = c("barcode", "is_cell", "contig_id", "high_confidence", "full_length",
                            "productive", "chain", "cdr3", "cdr3_nt", "v_gene", "j_gene",
                            "reads", "umis", "raw_clonotype_id", "origin"))
cat("contigs:", nrow(contigs), " cells:", uniqueN(contigs$barcode), "\n")
contigs[, .N, by = .(is_cell, productive, full_length, high_confidence)]
contigs[, .N, by = chain]
quantile(contigs$umis, c(0, .01, .05, .1, .25, .5, .75, .9, .99, 1))
contigs[, .(n = .N, umi1 = round(100 * mean(umis == 1), 1), umi2 = round(100 * mean(umis == 2), 1),
            umi3plus = round(100 * mean(umis >= 3), 1)), by = chain]
```

GEO provides only Cell Ranger's *filtered* contig file, so every contig already passes the four
flags. UMI support is the filter that matters. Only 0.7% of TRB contigs have a single UMI, but
4.8% of TRA contigs have 1 UMI and 9.3% have 2.

### Is this a noisy run? (2 vs 3 UMIs)

Ambient contigs, mostly from highly expanded clones, usually show up as an *extra* chain in a cell
(not its top-UMI chain of that type) whose CDR3 belongs to an expanded clone in the same library.
If 2-UMI contigs show that pattern much like 1-UMI contigs, the 3-UMI cutoff is warranted.

```{r}
#| label: vdj-ambient-check
contigs[, umi_rank := frank(-umis, ties.method = "first"), by = .(barcode, chain)]
contigs[, extra_chain := umi_rank > 1]

# Expanded CDR3s: seen as the top chain in >= 10 cells of the same library
top_cdr3 <- contigs[umi_rank == 1, .(n_cells = uniqueN(barcode)), by = .(origin, chain, cdr3_nt)]
expanded <- top_cdr3[n_cells >= 10, .(origin, chain, cdr3_nt)]
contigs[, from_expanded := FALSE]
contigs[expanded, from_expanded := TRUE, on = .(origin, chain, cdr3_nt)]

contigs[, umi_bin := fcase(umis == 1, "1", umis == 2, "2", umis == 3, "3", umis <= 5, "4-5", default = "6+")]
amb <- contigs[, .(contigs = .N,
                   pct_extra_chain        = round(100 * mean(extra_chain), 1),
                   pct_expanded_cdr3      = round(100 * mean(from_expanded), 1),
                   pct_extra_and_expanded = round(100 * mean(extra_chain & from_expanded), 1)),
               by = .(chain, umi_bin)][order(chain, umi_bin)]
amb
rm(top_cdr3, expanded); invisible(gc())
```

It isn't noisy. Extra chains from expanded clones are ≤2.3% of contigs in every UMI bin, and
2-UMI contigs aren't meaningfully worse than 3-UMI ones (TRA 2.3% vs 1.6%; TRB 0.5% vs 0.5%).
So we use the standard 2-UMI cutoff. Most low-UMI contigs are the cell's *only* chain of that
type, so the filter mainly costs some cells their TRA rather than removing ambient chains.

### Filter contigs and rebuild per-cell TCR columns

```{r}
#| label: vdj-filter
min_umi <- 2
n_before <- nrow(contigs)
vdj <- contigs[is_cell & productive & full_length & high_confidence & umis >= min_umi]
cat("contigs kept:", nrow(vdj), "of", n_before, sprintf("(%.1f%%)", 100 * nrow(vdj) / n_before), "\n")
contigs[umis < min_umi, .N, by = chain]
rm(contigs); invisible(gc())
```

```{r}
#| label: vdj-per-cell
setorder(vdj, barcode, chain, -umis)
vdj_cells <- vdj[, .(
  tcr_n_TRA      = sum(chain == "TRA"),
  tcr_n_TRB      = sum(chain == "TRB"),
  tcr_TRA_cdr3   = paste(cdr3[chain == "TRA"], collapse = ";"),   # ordered by UMI, high to low
  tcr_TRB_cdr3   = paste(cdr3[chain == "TRB"], collapse = ";"),
  tcr_TRA_umis   = paste(umis[chain == "TRA"], collapse = ";"),
  tcr_TRB_umis   = paste(umis[chain == "TRB"], collapse = ";"),
  tcr_TRA1_nt    = cdr3_nt[chain == "TRA"][1],                    # top-UMI chain of each type
  tcr_TRB1_nt    = cdr3_nt[chain == "TRB"][1],
  tcr_TRA1_v     = v_gene[chain == "TRA"][1],
  tcr_TRB1_v     = v_gene[chain == "TRB"][1],
  tcr_clonotype_cr = raw_clonotype_id[1]
), by = .(tcr_barcode = barcode)]
vdj_cells[tcr_TRA_cdr3 == "", `:=`(tcr_TRA_cdr3 = NA, tcr_TRA_umis = NA)]
vdj_cells[tcr_TRB_cdr3 == "", `:=`(tcr_TRB_cdr3 = NA, tcr_TRB_umis = NA)]
vdj_cells[, tcr_multichain := tcr_n_TRB > 1 | tcr_n_TRA > 2]
rm(vdj); invisible(gc())

vdj_cells[, .N, by = .(tcr_n_TRA, tcr_n_TRB)][order(-N)]
```

`tcr_clonotype_cr` is Cell Ranger's clonotype, which was built from the *unfiltered* chains. For
clonotype analyses after this filter, prefer a key built from the kept chains (e.g. donor +
`tcr_TRB1_nt` + `tcr_TRA1_nt`).

### Attach to GEX-QC cells

```{r}
#| label: vdj-attach
old_tcr_cols <- c("has_tcr", "tcr_clonotype", "tcr_n_TRA", "tcr_n_TRB", "tcr_TRA_cdr3", "tcr_TRB_cdr3")
attach_vdj <- function(obj) {
  for (col in intersect(old_tcr_cols, colnames(obj[[]]))) obj[[col]] <- NULL
  m <- vdj_cells[data.table(tcr_barcode = obj$tcr_barcode), on = "tcr_barcode"]
  stopifnot(identical(m$tcr_barcode, unname(obj$tcr_barcode)))
  m[, `:=`(tcr_has_TRB = !is.na(tcr_n_TRB) & tcr_n_TRB >= 1,
           tcr_paired  = !is.na(tcr_n_TRB) & tcr_n_TRB >= 1 & tcr_n_TRA >= 1)]
  m[is.na(tcr_multichain), tcr_multichain := FALSE]
  m <- as.data.frame(m[, !"tcr_barcode"])
  rownames(m) <- colnames(obj)
  AddMetaData(obj, m)
}
pre  <- attach_vdj(pre)
post <- attach_vdj(post)
vdj_in_gex <- vdj_cells[, mean(tcr_barcode %in% c(pre$tcr_barcode, post$tcr_barcode))]
cat(sprintf("VDJ cells kept after GEX QC: %.1f%%\n", 100 * vdj_in_gex))
rm(attach_vdj, old_tcr_cols, vdj_in_gex); invisible(gc())
```

### Recovery

Recovery is the share of GEX-QC cells with a productive TRB, and the share with a paired TRA +
TRB.

```{r}
#| label: vdj-recovery
recovery <- function(o, by) {
  d <- as.data.table(o[[]])
  d[, .(cells = .N,
        pct_TRB        = round(100 * mean(tcr_has_TRB), 1),
        pct_paired     = round(100 * mean(tcr_paired), 1),
        pct_multichain = round(100 * mean(tcr_multichain), 1)), by = by][order(get(by[1]))]
}
cat("== Overall\n");       print(rbind(recovery(pre, "stage"), recovery(post, "stage")))
cat("== PRE by sample\n");  print(recovery(pre, "orig.ident"))
cat("== POST by sample\n"); print(recovery(post, "orig.ident"))
cat("== By cell type\n")
print(rbind(recovery(pre, c("stage", "Final_celltype")), recovery(post, c("stage", "Final_celltype"))))
```

"doubleNeg" cells mostly lack a TRB (15–28%). They're probably γδ T cells or non-T cells, not
αβ T cells, so αβ recovery is reported for CD4 + CD8 cells only:

```{r}
#| label: vdj-recovery-ab
ab <- function(o) {
  d <- as.data.table(o[[]])[Final_celltype %in% c("CD4", "CD8")]
  d[, .(cells = .N, pct_TRB = round(100 * mean(tcr_has_TRB), 1),
        pct_paired = round(100 * mean(tcr_paired), 1),
        pct_multichain = round(100 * mean(tcr_multichain), 1)), by = stage]
}
rbind(ab(pre), ab(post))
```

```{r}
#| label: vdj-cleanup
#| cache: false
fwrite(vdj_cells, file.path(proc_dir, "vdj_cells_qc.csv.gz"))
rm(vdj_cells, recovery, ab, min_umi, n_before, amb); invisible(gc())
```

### VDJ QC summary

- **Contigs:** 146,260 of 150,378 kept (97.3%). The 4,118 removed had 1 UMI (3,604 TRA, 514 TRB).
- **GEX match:** 87.9% of QC'd VDJ cells match a cell that passed GEX QC.
- **Recovery, all GEX-QC cells:** pre-infusion 91.9% with TRB / 86.0% paired; post-infusion
  86.9% / 74.9%.
- **Recovery, αβ T cells (CD4 + CD8):** pre-infusion 95.9% with TRB / 90.3% paired (18,462
  cells); post-infusion 90.2% / 77.9% (47,698 cells).
- **Multi-chain flag:** 1.8–2.0% of cells. scDblFinder had already removed about half of the
  multi-TRB cells.
- **Weak samples:** `116-d21` (14.4% TRB), `039-d10` (53.5% TRB, 18.0% paired), `116-d28`
  (58.8% TRB). These match the small TCR libraries noted earlier.

### Caveat: what TCR overlap can and can't tell us

::: {.callout-warning}
**These products are autologous, and the GEO post-infusion data is (almost) all CAR+ cells.**

- **Autologous:** the CAR-T product is made from the patient's own T cells, so the patient's
  unengineered T cells can carry the same TCRs as product cells. TCR sequence alone can't
  separate product-derived cells from the patient's own cells.
- **Study design:** after infusion, cells were stained with BV421 anti-CD3ε (SK7) and AF647
  CD19 tetramers. They
  were then sorted into CAR T cells (CD3+ CAR+) and endogenous T cells (CD3+ CAR−), each run as
  a separate 10x library (Methods). So the study *did* capture unengineered T cells after
  infusion.
- **What's in the GEO processed data:** 20 of 22 post-infusion libraries are labelled as CAR T
  (`-CART`, `-CAR`, `-carT`). Only two tiny libraries are labelled `nonT`: `028-d04-nonT`
  (25 cells, removed in QC) and `033-d10-nonT` (20 cells). These are plausibly CD3+CAR− sorts,
  but that is unconfirmed, and the TCR table labels both as `-CART`. In practice, the processed
  post-infusion data is CAR+ cells only. The endogenous libraries may be in the raw SRA data.
- **What follows:** within this data, pre → post clonotype overlap measures how product clones
  persist and expand. It doesn't identify *which* post-infusion cells came from the product,
  because essentially all of them did. A post-infusion clone with no pre-infusion match is not
  evidence of an endogenous origin; it more likely reflects how deeply the product was sampled.
  An endogenous comparator would need the CD3+CAR− libraries from the raw data.
- **Contrast with allogeneic products:** there, donor and host repertoires barely overlap, so TCR
  overlap alone identifies product cells. That reasoning doesn't carry over to this dataset.
:::

### The CAR and CD3 ADT signals are missing after infusion

Sorted CAR+ cells should show *more* CAR ADT signal, not less. Instead, CAR is almost absent after
infusion, and so is CD3E.

First, check that the post-infusion ADT labels are correct. Each protein should correlate best
with its own gene:

```{r}
#| label: adt-label-check
adt_rna_pairs <- c(CD4 = "CD4", CD8A = "CD8A", CD5 = "CD5", CD25 = "IL2RA", `PD-1` = "PDCD1",
                   CD27 = "CD27", CD28 = "CD28", TIGIT = "TIGIT", CD39 = "ENTPD1", CD95 = "FAS",
                   CXCR3 = "CXCR3", CCR4 = "CCR4", `4-1BB` = "TNFRSF9")
adt_label_check <- function(o, n = 8000) {
  set.seed(1); cells <- sample(colnames(o), min(n, ncol(o)))
  adt <- as.matrix(LayerData(o, assay = "ADT", layer = "data")[, cells])
  rna <- as.matrix(LayerData(o, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")[adt_rna_pairs, cells])
  cm  <- cor(t(adt), t(rna), method = "spearman"); cm[is.na(cm)] <- 0
  data.table(gene = adt_rna_pairs, expected_adt = names(adt_rna_pairs),
             r_expected = round(cm[cbind(names(adt_rna_pairs), adt_rna_pairs)], 2),
             best_adt = rownames(cm)[apply(cm, 2, which.max)])
}
cat("== PRE\n");  print(adt_label_check(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(adt_label_check(post))
rm(adt_rna_pairs, adt_label_check); invisible(gc())
```

They are: in both stages each protein's best-correlated gene is its own. So the low CAR signal
isn't a labelling shift, even though the protein *order* differs between the two GEO name files.

Next, compare CAR and CD3E with the isotype controls. An antibody in the staining mix always
leaves some background counts, so a reagent far *below* the isotype controls was most likely
not in the staining mix, not read out, or completely blocked.

```{r}
#| label: car-adt-check
adt_presence <- function(o) {
  m <- LayerData(o, assay = "ADT", layer = "counts")[c("CD3E", "CAR", "IgG1", "IgG2a", "IgG2b"), ]
  d <- data.table(sample = o$orig.ident, t(as.matrix(m > 0)))
  d[, lapply(.SD, function(x) round(100 * mean(x), 1)), by = sample][order(sample)]
}
cat("== PRE: % of cells with any counts\n");  print(adt_presence(pre))
cat("== POST: % of cells with any counts\n"); print(adt_presence(post))
rm(adt_presence); invisible(gc())
```

- **After infusion, in every sample:** CD3E and CAR are nonzero in only 0–2.4% of cells, while
  isotype controls are nonzero in 13–100%. So both are effectively unmeasured.
- **Before infusion:** CD3E is present in every sample, but CAR only in the P-prefixed samples
  (P033 and P034 ~100% nonzero, P049 69%). In 031, 039 and 116 it is below the isotype controls
  too.

The Methods (CITE-seq antibody preparation) explain most of this:

- **CD3E wasn't stained after infusion.** The panel has 31 TotalSeq-C reagents: 28 antibodies
  plus 3 isotype controls. Residual infusion product was stained with all 31. Patient PBMCs
  (post-infusion) were stained with 30: anti-CD3ε (UCHT1) was *left out*, because those cells
  were stained with BV421 anti-CD3ε (SK7) for sorting. The residual CD3E counts after infusion
  are background.
- **"CAR" isn't one of the 31 documented reagents.** The GEO matrix has 32 ADT features, so
  "CAR" is an extra, undocumented feature. Its signal appears only in the pre-infusion
  P-prefixed batch. What it measures is unknown (possibly a DNA-barcoded CD19 reagent used in
  some samples only, but that's a guess), so treat it as unusable unless the authors clarify.
  The CD19 tetramer used for sorting is listed as AF647-labelled, not oligo-barcoded.

**Consequences:**

- **Post-infusion CAR+ status** can't be checked at the protein level. The RNA does measure the
  CAR transgene, though (`YESCAR`, see *CAR transgene RNA* below).
- **Drop from the post-infusion ADT assay:** CAR and CD3E, then re-run CLR (below).
- **Before infusion:** CAR is kept in the assay but shouldn't be used. It's undocumented, and
  present only in P033/P034/P049. Don't compare it across stages or batches.
- **A third sign of two pre-infusion batches:** the CAR feature, alongside the naming and mito
  differences.

### Drop CAR and CD3E from the post-infusion ADT assay

CLR scales each cell by the geometric mean across its proteins, so the two unmeasured features
are removed before normalizing again. `nCount_ADT` and `nFeature_ADT` are recomputed to match.

```{r}
#| label: adt-drop-post
adt_drop_post <- c("CAR", "CD3E")
post[["ADT"]] <- subset(post[["ADT"]], features = setdiff(rownames(post[["ADT"]]), adt_drop_post))

adt_counts <- LayerData(post, assay = "ADT", layer = "counts")
post$nCount_ADT   <- colSums(adt_counts)
post$nFeature_ADT <- colSums(adt_counts > 0)
rm(adt_counts)
post <- NormalizeData(post, assay = "ADT", normalization.method = "CLR", margin = 2, verbose = FALSE)
DefaultAssay(post) <- "RNA"

stopifnot(nrow(post[["ADT"]]) == 30, !any(adt_drop_post %in% rownames(post[["ADT"]])),
          identical(rownames(LayerData(post, assay = "ADT", layer = "data")),
                    rownames(LayerData(post, assay = "ADT", layer = "counts"))))
rm(adt_drop_post); invisible(gc())
```
- **"nonT" samples:** two post-infusion samples are named "nonT" (`033-d10-nonT`, 20 cells,
  kept; `028-d04-nonT`, removed in QC). Their sort gate may differ, so consider excluding them
  from clonotype analyses.

## Remove non-T contamination

In the first variable-gene pass, monocyte genes (S100A8/9/12, LYZ, CST3, C1QA) and platelet genes
(PPBP, PF4, GP9) topped the post-infusion list. Sorted CD3+ cells shouldn't express them, so the
cells carrying them are measured and removed here.

### Monocyte-like cells

```{r}
#| label: qc-myeloid
myeloid_genes <- c("LYZ", "S100A8", "S100A9", "CST3", "FCN1", "CD14")
tcell_genes   <- c("CD3E", "CD3D", "CD3G", "TRAC", "TRBC1", "TRBC2", "CD2")
max_myeloid_pct <- 0.2

flag_myeloid <- function(o) {
  cnt <- LayerData(o, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  o$myeloid_pct <- 100 * colSums(cnt[myeloid_genes, ]) / o$nCount_RNA
  o$tcell_pct   <- 100 * colSums(cnt[tcell_genes, ])   / o$nCount_RNA
  o$qc_myeloid  <- o$myeloid_pct > max_myeloid_pct
  o
}
pre  <- flag_myeloid(pre)
post <- flag_myeloid(post)

myeloid_summary <- function(o) {
  d <- as.data.table(o[[]])
  d[, .(cells = .N, myeloid_flagged = sum(qc_myeloid), pct = round(100 * mean(qc_myeloid), 1),
        flagged_med_tcell_pct = round(median(tcell_pct[qc_myeloid]), 2),
        flagged_pct_TRB = round(100 * mean(tcr_has_TRB[qc_myeloid]), 1)), by = orig.ident][order(orig.ident)]
}
cat("== PRE\n");  print(myeloid_summary(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(myeloid_summary(post))
```

Cells above 0.2% monocyte UMIs have a median of **zero** T-cell gene expression (CD3, TRAC, TRBC,
CD2). Only 12–15% have a TCR, so they are monocytes that got past the sort, not T cells. Many
carry the authors' "CD4" label, since monocytes express CD4 protein. They're concentrated in
patients 116 (12–53% of cells), 048 (9–28%), 039 and 031. Patients 033, 034 and 049 have none.
This explains the low TCR recovery in `116-d21` and `116-d28`. In patient 048, 20–56% of flagged
cells do have a TCR, so many are probably T-cell/monocyte doublets; they're removed either way.

### Platelet-bound cells

Platelets stuck to T cells are rare, but they put spiky platelet genes into the variable-gene
list. Cells with ≥5 platelet UMIs are removed (232 post-infusion, 5 pre-infusion).

```{r}
#| label: qc-platelet
platelet_genes <- c("PPBP", "PF4", "GP9", "TUBB1", "NRGN", "RGS18", "PTCRA", "CMTM5")
min_platelet_umi <- 5
flag_platelet <- function(o) {
  o$platelet_umi <- colSums(LayerData(o, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")[platelet_genes, ])
  o$qc_platelet  <- o$platelet_umi >= min_platelet_umi
  o
}
pre  <- flag_platelet(pre)
post <- flag_platelet(post)
rbind(pre = table(pre$qc_platelet), post = table(post$qc_platelet))
```

```{r}
#| label: qc-contam-save-flags
#| cache: false
qc_flags <- fread(file.path(proc_dir, "qc_flags.csv.gz"))
contam <- rbind(
  data.table(cell = colnames(pre),  myeloid_pct = pre$myeloid_pct,  qc_myeloid = pre$qc_myeloid,
             platelet_umi = pre$platelet_umi,  qc_platelet = pre$qc_platelet),
  data.table(cell = colnames(post), myeloid_pct = post$myeloid_pct, qc_myeloid = post$qc_myeloid,
             platelet_umi = post$platelet_umi, qc_platelet = post$qc_platelet))
qc_flags <- contam[qc_flags, on = "cell"]
qc_flags[, qc_pass := qc_pass & !fcoalesce(qc_myeloid, FALSE) & !fcoalesce(qc_platelet, FALSE)]
fwrite(qc_flags, file.path(proc_dir, "qc_flags.csv.gz"))
rm(qc_flags, contam)

pre  <- subset(pre,  cells = colnames(pre)[!pre$qc_myeloid & !pre$qc_platelet])
post <- subset(post, cells = colnames(post)[!post$qc_myeloid & !post$qc_platelet])
rm(flag_myeloid, myeloid_summary, myeloid_genes, tcell_genes, max_myeloid_pct,
   flag_platelet, platelet_genes, min_platelet_umi); invisible(gc())
c(pre = ncol(pre), post = ncol(post))
```

### CAR transgene RNA (`YESCAR`)

The RNA matrix has 33,539 features: the 33,538 genes of 10x's GRCh38 v3.0.0 reference, plus
`YESCAR` as the last feature. This is presumably the axi-cel (Yescarta) CAR transgene, added to
the reference. Unlike the ADT data, it gives a direct CAR measurement.

```{r}
#| label: car-rna
car_rna <- function(o) {
  x <- LayerData(o, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")["YESCAR", ]
  d <- data.table(sample = o$orig.ident, car = x)
  rbind(d[, .(cells = .N, pct_pos = round(100 * mean(car > 0), 1), median = median(car),
              p90 = as.numeric(quantile(car, .9))), by = sample][order(sample)],
        d[, .(sample = "TOTAL", cells = .N, pct_pos = round(100 * mean(car > 0), 1), median = median(car),
              p90 = as.numeric(quantile(car, .9)))])
}
match("YESCAR", rownames(pre))
cat("== PRE\n");  print(car_rna(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(car_rna(post))
rm(car_rna)
```

- **Pre-infusion:** 48% of cells have CAR RNA (40–64% per sample). That fits a product mixing
  transduced and untransduced T cells.
- **Post-infusion:** 56% overall. Detection is limited by dropout: these cells are sequenced ~3×
  more shallowly and carry fewer CAR transcripts (90th percentile 3 vs 16 UMIs). So zero CAR
  counts doesn't mean a cell is CAR−. Some samples are lower still: 039 (17–31%) and `116-d21`
  (10%), possibly from lower CAR expression or some sort impurity.
- **`033-d10-nonT`:** 0 of 20 cells have CAR RNA, so it's almost certainly an endogenous
  (CD3+CAR−) sort. It's removed from the CAR-T object:

```{r}
#| label: drop-nonT
post <- subset(post, cells = colnames(post)[post$orig.ident != "033-d10-nonT"])
post$orig.ident <- droplevels(post$orig.ident)
invisible(gc())
c(pre = ncol(pre), post = ncol(post))
```

## Variable genes and PCA

Per stage: 2,000 variable genes (vst), excluding the following, then scaling and 50 PCs.

- **TCR V/J/C segments:** they track clonotype, not cell state.
- **`MTRNR2L` pseudogenes:** mito-like artefacts.
- **Hemoglobin genes:** rare red-cell contamination.

`YESCAR` is kept as a variable gene, since CAR expression level is biology of interest.

```{r}
#| label: hvg-pca
hvg_exclude_re <- "^TR[ABDG][VJC]|^MTRNR2L|^HB[AB]\\d?$"

hvg_pca <- function(o, n_hvg = 2000, n_pcs = 50) {
  o <- FindVariableFeatures(o, assay = "RNA", selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = n_hvg + 300,
                            verbose = FALSE)
  hvg <- VariableFeatures(o)
  hvg <- head(hvg[!grepl(hvg_exclude_re, hvg)], n_hvg)
  VariableFeatures(o) <- hvg
  o <- ScaleData(o, assay = "RNA", features = hvg, verbose = FALSE)
  o <- RunPCA(o, assay = "RNA", features = hvg, npcs = n_pcs, verbose = FALSE)
  o
}
pre  <- hvg_pca(pre);  invisible(gc())
post <- hvg_pca(post); invisible(gc())
cat("PRE top 25 HVGs: ",  paste(head(VariableFeatures(pre), 25),  collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("POST top 25 HVGs:", paste(head(VariableFeatures(post), 25), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

Pre-infusion's top variable genes are cytokines and chemokines (IL17F, CSF2, IFNG, IL5, IL13, CCL3/4),
as expected for an activated product. Post-infusion's are proliferation genes (histones, MKI67, TOP2A,
UBE2C).

### How much do sample and patient drive the PCs?

```{r}
#| label: pc-batch-r2
pc_r2 <- function(o, vars, n = 10) {
  pcs <- Embeddings(o, "pca")[, 1:n]
  md  <- o[[]]
  r2  <- sapply(vars, function(v) apply(pcs, 2, function(p) summary(lm(p ~ factor(md[[v]])))$r.squared))
  data.table(PC = 1:n, var_explained = round(100 * (Stdev(o, "pca")[1:n]^2) / sum(Stdev(o, "pca")^2), 1),
             round(r2, 2))
}
pre$pre_batch <- ifelse(grepl("^P", as.character(pre$orig.ident)), "P-batch", "other")
cat("== PRE: R^2 of each PC vs sample / batch / cell type\n")
print(pc_r2(pre,  c("orig.ident", "pre_batch", "Final_celltype")))
cat("== POST: R^2 of each PC vs sample / patient / day / cell type\n")
print(pc_r2(post, c("orig.ident", "patient", "time", "Final_celltype")))
```

PC1 is largely independent of sample in both stages (R² ≤ 0.24). Several of the following PCs
are dominated by sample and patient: pre-infusion PC2 (R² 0.67 with sample), and post-infusion PCs 3–6
(R² 0.46–0.70 with sample, 0.23–0.62 with patient). So clustering needs integration.

## Integration (Harmony by patient)

Harmony on the first 30 PCs, correcting for **patient**, not sample. Patient-level correction
removes differences between patients but keeps day-to-day changes within each patient, which is
the post-infusion biology of interest. In pre-infusion, patient also covers the P-vs-other
processing batch, since the two overlap completely.

```{r}
#| label: harmony
library(harmony)
n_dims <- 30
set.seed(1)
pre  <- RunHarmony(pre,  group.by.vars = "patient", reduction.use = "pca", dims.use = 1:n_dims,
                   reduction.save = "harmony", verbose = FALSE)
set.seed(1)
post <- RunHarmony(post, group.by.vars = "patient", reduction.use = "pca", dims.use = 1:n_dims,
                   reduction.save = "harmony", verbose = FALSE)
invisible(gc())

emb_r2 <- function(o, red, vars, n = 10) {
  e  <- Embeddings(o, red)[, 1:n]
  md <- o[[]]
  data.table(dim = 1:n, round(sapply(vars, function(v)
    apply(e, 2, function(p) summary(lm(p ~ factor(md[[v]])))$r.squared)), 2))
}
cat("== PRE  patient R^2, PCA vs Harmony\n")
print(cbind(emb_r2(pre, "pca", "patient"), harmony = emb_r2(pre, "harmony", "patient")$patient))
cat("== POST patient & day R^2, PCA vs Harmony\n")
p1 <- emb_r2(post, "pca", c("patient", "time")); p2 <- emb_r2(post, "harmony", c("patient", "time"))
print(data.table(dim = 1:10, pca_patient = p1$patient, harmony_patient = p2$patient,
                 pca_day = p1$time, harmony_day = p2$time))
rm(p1, p2); invisible(gc())
```

- **Patient effect removed:** patient R² falls from up to 0.67 to ≤0.18 (pre-infusion) and from
  up to 0.62 to ≤0.09 (post-infusion).
- **Day effect partly kept:** R² for day falls from 0.12–0.37 to 0.11–0.22 on post-infusion
  dimensions 2–6. Some loss is expected, because days aren't sampled evenly across patients.

## Clustering and UMAP

```{r}
#| label: cluster
resolutions <- c(0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0)
cluster_umap <- function(o) {
  o <- FindNeighbors(o, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:n_dims, verbose = FALSE)
  o <- FindClusters(o, resolution = resolutions, verbose = FALSE)
  o <- RunUMAP(o, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:n_dims, reduction.name = "umap", verbose = FALSE)
  o
}
pre  <- cluster_umap(pre);  invisible(gc())
post <- cluster_umap(post); invisible(gc())
n_clusters <- function(o) sapply(paste0("RNA_snn_res.", resolutions), function(r) nlevels(o[[r, drop = TRUE]]))
rbind(pre = n_clusters(pre), post = n_clusters(post))
```

### Remove non-T clusters

Clusters where few cells have a TCR or express CD3 are non-T cells. TCR + CD3 + CAR RNA per
cluster:

```{r}
#| label: cluster-tcell-check
cluster_tcell_stats <- function(o, res = "RNA_snn_res.0.5") {
  cnt <- LayerData(o, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  d <- data.table(cluster = o[[res, drop = TRUE]], has_TRB = o$tcr_has_TRB,
                  cd3 = colSums(cnt[c("CD3E", "CD3D", "CD3G"), ]) > 0, car = cnt["YESCAR", ] > 0)
  d[, .(cells = .N, pct_TRB = round(100 * mean(has_TRB), 1), pct_CD3 = round(100 * mean(cd3), 1),
        pct_CAR_rna = round(100 * mean(car), 1)), by = cluster][order(cluster)]
}
ct_pre  <- cluster_tcell_stats(pre);  print(ct_pre)
ct_post <- cluster_tcell_stats(post); print(ct_post)

nonT_pre  <- ct_pre[pct_TRB < 25 & pct_CD3 < 50, as.character(cluster)]
nonT_post <- ct_post[pct_TRB < 25 & pct_CD3 < 50, as.character(cluster)]
cat("non-T clusters: pre", nonT_pre, "| post", nonT_post, "\n")
n_nonT_pre  <- sum(as.character(pre$RNA_snn_res.0.5)  %in% nonT_pre)
n_nonT_post <- sum(as.character(post$RNA_snn_res.0.5) %in% nonT_post)
```

```{r}
#| label: nonT-cluster-markers
top_markers <- function(o, cl, res = "RNA_snn_res.0.5", n = 15) {
  Idents(o) <- res
  m <- FindMarkers(o, ident.1 = cl, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = 0.5,
                   max.cells.per.ident = 1500, verbose = FALSE)
  m <- m[order(-m$avg_log2FC), ]
  m <- head(m[m$p_val_adj < 0.01, ], n)
  paste0(rownames(m), " (", round(m$avg_log2FC, 1), ")", collapse = ", ")
}
for (cl in nonT_pre)  cat("PRE  cluster", cl, ":", top_markers(pre,  cl), "\n")
for (cl in nonT_post) cat("POST cluster", cl, ":", top_markers(post, cl), "\n")
```

- **Pre-infusion (`r n_nonT_pre` cells):** dendritic-cell and macrophage genes (CCL19, CCL22, IDO1, HCK,
  MS4A7). 9% have a TCR, 22% express CD3, 4% have CAR RNA.
- **Post-infusion (`r n_nonT_post` cells):** NK-cell genes (KLRF1, NCR1, SH2D1B, TYROBP, FCER1G; TRDC RNA is
  also expressed in NK cells). 4% have a TCR, 44% express CD3, and 3% have CAR RNA vs 56%
  overall. So these are NK cells that got through the sort, *not* NK-like CAR T cells.

```{r}
#| label: drop-nonT-clusters
#| cache: false
cat("non-T clusters -- pre:", if (length(nonT_pre)) nonT_pre else "none",
    "| post:", if (length(nonT_post)) nonT_post else "none", "\n")
pre$qc_nonT_cluster  <- as.character(pre$RNA_snn_res.0.5)  %in% nonT_pre
post$qc_nonT_cluster <- as.character(post$RNA_snn_res.0.5) %in% nonT_post

qc_flags <- fread(file.path(proc_dir, "qc_flags.csv.gz"))
nt <- rbind(data.table(cell = colnames(pre),  qc_nonT_cluster = pre$qc_nonT_cluster),
            data.table(cell = colnames(post), qc_nonT_cluster = post$qc_nonT_cluster))
qc_flags <- nt[qc_flags, on = "cell"]
qc_flags[orig.ident == "033-d10-nonT", qc_pass := FALSE]
qc_flags[, qc_pass := qc_pass & !fcoalesce(qc_nonT_cluster, FALSE)]
fwrite(qc_flags, file.path(proc_dir, "qc_flags.csv.gz"))
rm(list = intersect(c("qc_flags","nt","ct_pre","ct_post","nonT_pre","nonT_post","cl"), ls()))

pre  <- subset(pre,  cells = colnames(pre)[!pre$qc_nonT_cluster])
post <- subset(post, cells = colnames(post)[!post$qc_nonT_cluster])
invisible(gc())
```

Then rebuild the embedding without them: variable genes → PCA → Harmony → clusters → UMAP.

```{r}
#| label: rerun-embedding
rerun <- function(o) {
  o <- hvg_pca(o)
  set.seed(1)
  o <- RunHarmony(o, group.by.vars = "patient", reduction.use = "pca", dims.use = 1:n_dims,
                  reduction.save = "harmony", verbose = FALSE)
  cluster_umap(o)
}
pre  <- rerun(pre);  invisible(gc())
post <- rerun(post); invisible(gc())
rbind(pre = n_clusters(pre), post = n_clusters(post))
c(pre = ncol(pre), post = ncol(post))
```

The cell counts (`r fmt_n(ncol(pre))` pre, `r fmt_n(ncol(post))` post) match the `qc_pass` totals in `qc_flags.csv.gz`.

### Final cluster checks

```{r}
#| label: cluster-tcell-check-final
cluster_tcell_stats <- function(o, res = "RNA_snn_res.0.5") {
  cnt <- LayerData(o, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  d <- data.table(cluster = o[[res, drop = TRUE]], patient = o$patientShort, has_TRB = o$tcr_has_TRB,
                  cd3 = colSums(cnt[c("CD3E", "CD3D", "CD3G"), ]) > 0, car = cnt["YESCAR", ] > 0)
  d[, .(cells = .N, pct_TRB = round(100 * mean(has_TRB), 1), pct_CD3 = round(100 * mean(cd3), 1),
        pct_CAR_rna = round(100 * mean(car), 1),
        top_patient_pct = round(100 * max(table(patient)) / .N, 1)), by = cluster][order(cluster)]
}
cat("== PRE\n");  print(cluster_tcell_stats(pre))
cat("== POST\n"); print(cluster_tcell_stats(post))
```

Two clusters stand out:

- **Pre-infusion cluster 8 (337 cells): γδ T and NK cells, kept.** 77% express TRDC and 27% TRGV9;
  NK genes (KIR2DL4, KLRF1, NCR1, NCAM1, FCGR3A) are common. Only 2% have a TCRβ and 5% have
  CAR RNA. The infusion product wasn't CAR-sorted, so these untransduced cells are a genuine
  part of the product. They're kept and labelled at annotation, unlike the post-infusion NK
  cells, which got through a CD3+CAR+ sort.
- **Post-infusion cluster 6 (1,583 cells): likely low quality, flagged (`flag_lowq_cluster`).** Its top
  markers are long, general-purpose genes (ATXN1, CREBBP, RICTOR, KLF12, ARID1B). Compared with
  other cells, it has half the UMIs (median 2,195 vs 3,980), about twice the mito % (5.3 vs 2.8)
  and lower TCRβ (49%) and CAR RNA (33%) detection. Removal is to be decided at annotation.

```{r}
#| label: cluster-qc-checks
gd_nk_check <- function(o, cl) {
  cells <- colnames(o)[o$RNA_snn_res.0.5 == cl]
  rest  <- setdiff(colnames(o), cells)
  cnt <- LayerData(o, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  pos <- function(g, cc) round(100 * mean(colSums(cnt[intersect(g, rownames(cnt)), cc, drop = FALSE]) > 0), 1)
  genes <- list(TRDC = "TRDC", `TRGC1/2` = c("TRGC1", "TRGC2"), TRGV9 = "TRGV9", TRAC = "TRAC",
                `KLRF1/NCR1` = c("KLRF1", "NCR1"), YESCAR = "YESCAR")
  data.table(marker = names(genes), cluster = sapply(genes, pos, cells), rest = sapply(genes, pos, rest))
}
cat("== PRE cluster 8\n"); print(gd_nk_check(pre, "8"))
cat("PRE cluster 8 markers:", top_markers(pre, "8", n = 12), "\n")

cat("POST cluster 6 markers:", top_markers(post, "6", n = 12), "\n")
as.data.table(post[[]])[, .(cl6 = RNA_snn_res.0.5 == "6", nCount_RNA, nFeature_RNA, percent.mt,
                            percent.ribo, dbl_score)][, lapply(.SD, function(x) round(median(x, na.rm = TRUE), 3)), by = cl6]

post$flag_lowq_cluster <- post$RNA_snn_res.0.5 == "6"
rm(gd_nk_check)
```

### Overview

```{r}
#| label: umap-plots
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9
pal8 <- c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#6250d6", "#e34948")
ct_cols <- c(CD4 = "#2a78d6", CD8 = "#eb6834", doubleNeg = "#1baf7a", doublePos = "#6250d6",
             undetermined = "#b8b7b1")
umap_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#0b0b0b"), legend.title = element_blank())

overview_plot <- function(o, title, res = "RNA_snn_res.0.5") {
  d <- data.table(Embeddings(o, "umap"), cluster = o[[res, drop = TRUE]], celltype = o$Final_celltype,
                  patient = o$patientShort)
  setnames(d, 1:2, c("u1", "u2"))
  d <- d[sample(.N)]
  lab <- d[, .(u1 = median(u1), u2 = median(u2)), by = cluster]
  p1 <- ggplot(d, aes(u1, u2)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = cluster), size = 0.05, alpha = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = rep(pal8, length.out = nlevels(d$cluster))) +
    geom_label(data = lab, aes(label = cluster), size = 3, linewidth = 0, fill = "#fcfcfb", alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(title = "Clusters (res 0.5)", x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2") + umap_theme
  p2 <- ggplot(d, aes(u1, u2, colour = celltype)) + geom_point(size = 0.05, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = ct_cols) + guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
    labs(title = "Authors' cell type (ADT-based)", x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2") + umap_theme
  comp <- d[, .N, by = .(cluster, patient)][, share := N / sum(N), by = cluster]
  p3 <- ggplot(comp, aes(x = cluster, y = share, fill = patient)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.8, colour = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal8) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(title = "Patient mix per cluster", x = "Cluster", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                                          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.title = element_blank())
  (p1 | p2) / p3 + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1)) +
    plot_annotation(title = title, theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)))
}
overview_plot(pre,  "Pre-infusion (Harmony by patient)")
overview_plot(post, "Post-infusion (Harmony by patient)")
```

- **Pre-infusion:** clusters are well mixed across patients. Cluster 9 (204 cells) is 66% P07.
- **Post-infusion:** CD4 cells sit apart from CD8. Cluster 7 (1,173 cells) is 83% P05 (patient 039).
  It's polyclonal T cells (top clone <1% in the earlier check), so it's a patient-specific state
  rather than one expanded clone, and Harmony doesn't merge it.

```{r}
#| label: embedding-cleanup
#| cache: false
rm(hvg_pca, pc_r2, emb_r2, rerun, cluster_umap, hvg_exclude_re, resolutions, n_clusters, n_dims)
invisible(gc())
saveRDS(pre,  file.path(proc_dir, "seurat_pre_infusion_clustered.rds"))
saveRDS(post, file.path(proc_dir, "seurat_post_infusion_clustered.rds"))
```

### Drop the low-quality post-infusion cluster

Post-infusion cluster 6 is removed. The existing embedding and cluster numbers are kept rather
than rebuilt, since it's 3.4% of cells and a rebuild would renumber every cluster.

```{r}
#| label: drop-lowq-cluster
#| cache: false
qc_flags <- fread(file.path(proc_dir, "qc_flags.csv.gz"))
qc_flags[, qc_lowq_cluster := cell %in% colnames(post)[post$flag_lowq_cluster]]
qc_flags[qc_lowq_cluster == TRUE, qc_pass := FALSE]
fwrite(qc_flags, file.path(proc_dir, "qc_flags.csv.gz"))
cat("cells passing all QC: pre", qc_flags[stage == "Pre", sum(qc_pass)], "| post", qc_flags[stage == "Post", sum(qc_pass)], "\n")
rm(qc_flags)

post <- subset(post, cells = colnames(post)[!post$flag_lowq_cluster])
post$flag_lowq_cluster <- NULL
for (r in grep("^RNA_snn_res", colnames(post[[]]), value = TRUE)) post[[r]] <- droplevels(post[[r, drop = TRUE]])
rm(r); invisible(gc())
c(post_cells = ncol(post), post_clusters_res0.5 = nlevels(post$RNA_snn_res.0.5))
```

## Annotation

Clusters at resolution 0.5 are annotated from four sources:

- **Surface proteins (ADT):** mean CLR per cluster, z-scored across clusters.
- **Canonical T-cell genes:** % of cells expressing each.
- **Cell-cycle phase.**
- **Unbiased markers:** `FindAllMarkers`, top 10 per cluster.

Clonal expansion is the share of TCRβ+ cells in clones of ≥5 cells, with clones defined
per patient by the top TRB CDR3 nucleotide sequence.

```{r}
#| label: annot-profile
adt_panel <- c("CD4", "CD8A", "CD45RA", "CD45RO", "CCR7", "CD27", "CD28", "CD95", "CD127", "CD25",
               "PD-1", "TIM-3", "LAG-3", "TIGIT", "CD39", "CD57", "CXCR3", "CCR4", "CCR6", "4-1BB", "OX40", "TCRgd")
rna_panel <- c("SELL", "TCF7", "LEF1", "IL7R", "GZMK", "GZMB", "PRF1", "GNLY", "NKG7", "FOXP3", "IL2RA",
               "MKI67", "TOP2A", "HAVCR2", "LAG3", "TOX", "ENTPD1", "KLRB1", "ZNF683", "CX3CR1", "KLRG1",
               "IFNG", "CSF2", "IL17A", "TRDC", "KLRF1", "YESCAR")

cluster_profile <- function(o, res = "RNA_snn_res.0.5") {
  cl  <- o[[res, drop = TRUE]]
  adt <- LayerData(o, assay = "ADT", layer = "data")
  adt_mean <- sapply(intersect(adt_panel, rownames(adt)), function(p) tapply(adt[p, ], cl, mean))
  adt_z    <- round(scale(adt_mean), 1)
  rna <- LayerData(o, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")[rna_panel, ]
  rna_pct  <- round(sapply(rna_panel, function(g) tapply(rna[g, ] > 0, cl, mean)) * 100)
  clone <- ifelse(o$tcr_has_TRB, paste(o$patient, o$tcr_TRB1_nt), NA)
  csize <- table(clone)
  big   <- !is.na(clone) & as.vector(csize[clone]) >= 5
  extra <- data.table(cluster = levels(cl), cells = as.vector(table(cl)),
                      pct_CD4_lab  = as.vector(round(100 * tapply(o$Final_celltype == "CD4", cl, mean))),
                      pct_CD8_lab  = as.vector(round(100 * tapply(o$Final_celltype == "CD8", cl, mean))),
                      pct_expanded = as.vector(round(100 * tapply(big[!is.na(clone)], cl[!is.na(clone)], mean))))
  list(extra = extra, adt_z = adt_z, rna_pct = rna_pct)
}
prof_pre  <- cluster_profile(pre)
prof_post <- cluster_profile(post)
prof_pre
prof_post
```

all_markers <- function(o, res = "RNA_snn_res.0.5", n = 10) {
  Idents(o) <- res
  m <- FindAllMarkers(o, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = 0.5,
                      max.cells.per.ident = 500, verbose = FALSE)
  m <- as.data.table(m)[p_val_adj < 0.01][order(cluster, -avg_log2FC)]
  m[, .(top = paste(head(gene, n), collapse = ", ")), by = cluster]
}

mk_post <- all_markers(post); mk_post
